# Data Engineering {.smaller .crunch-title .title-13 .ul-block .crunch-quarto-figure .crunch-img data-stack-name="Data Engineering"}

<div style="float: right;">

![@reis_fundamentals_2022, Figure 1-1 (p. 5)](images/lifecycle.png){.lightbox width="550"}

</div>

* Have you noticed? In most HWs, you've looked at `.parquet` **metadata** describing a column **schema**
* There's a whole book [@reis_fundamentals_2022], and a [whole job](https://trends.google.com/explore?q=data%20scientist%2C%20data%20engineer&date=2010-01-01%202026-10-01&geo=US), focused directly on facilitating seamless "flow" from raw data $\leadsto$ insights
* Today: **Streamline** separation and combination of (computation, data) by carefully defining and enforcing **schemas**
* Next week: Move to **full-on distributed computing** with **Spark!**<br>[*(...Much harder to debug issues with data flowing "out there" across EC2 nodes)*]{style="font-size: 90%;"}

## What is Data Engineering? {.crunch-title .text-75 .crunch-img .crunch-blockquote .crunch-p-6 .crunch-ul .ul-block}

<div style="float: right;">

![@reis_fundamentals_2022,<br>the [white-eared puffbird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-eared_puffbird) book](images/reis-cover.jpg){fig-align="center" width="360"}

</div>

> Data engineering is the development, implementation, and maintenance of systems  and processes that take in raw data and **produce** **high-quality**, **consistent** information that supports downstream use cases, such as analysis and machine learning [@reis_fundamentals_2022]

<div style="margin-bottom: 0px !important;">

Bolded terms $\Rightarrow$ new skills, tools in your toolkit:

</div>

* **Producers**, **consumers**: Who is responsible for what?
* Data **catalogs**: How does someone in your org *find* the data they're looking for, in their desired format?
* How is data **made available?** (Security, lifecycle management)

## What Do Data Engineers Do? {.title-09 .crunch-title .crunch-ul}

* **Disambiguation**: How to **interpret** what the data **means**?
  * <i class='bi bi-1-circle'></i> Register the **schema** within a data **catalog**
  * <i class='bi bi-2-circle'></i> Subject matter experts (*Data Stewards*) add meaningful descriptions
* **Deduplication**: Having a single source of truth!
* **Data Governance**: How long to store, access controls, etc.

Once this is done, data may be stored in a central repository such as a **data lake** or **data lakehouse**.

::: {.aside}

*Slide credit: Amit Arora!*

:::

## Reminder: Telemetry &rarr; Analytics

Recall how many tiny bits of information are **streaming into** a given app's servers at any given time!

> Database administrators therefore **closely guard their OLTP databases**. They are usually **reluctant to let business analysts run ad hoc analytic queries on an OLTP database**, since those queries are often expensive, scanning large parts of the dataset, which can harm the performance of concurrently executing transactions. [@kleppmann_designing_2026]

## Data Warehouse (Bill Inmon, 1989) {.crunch-title .text-90}

> Before the data warehouse, the analysis would often occur directly on the source system itself, with the obvious consequence of bogging down production **transactional** databases with long-running queries. The goal of the data warehouse was to separate the **source system [OLTP]** from the **analytical system [OLAP]**. [@reis_fundamentals_2022, p. 295]

> Data in the data warehouse is able to be used for many different purposes, including **sitting and waiting** for future requirements which are unknown today. [@inmon_building_2002]

## Data Warehouse Principles {.crunch-title .text-80 .crunch-ul}

* **Subject-oriented:** Focused on a specific subject area (sales, marketing)
* **Integrated:** Data from disparate sources is consolidated and normalized
* **Nonvolatile:** Data remains unchanged once stored
* **Time-variant:** Varying time ranges can be queried

![@reis_fundamentals_2022, Figure 8-13, p. 297](images/warehouse.png){fig-align="center"}

## Kimball Star Schema {.smaller .crunch-title .crunch-p}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}

![@kleppmann_designing_2026, pp. 77-79](images/star-schema.png){.lightbox fig-align="center" width="90%"}

:::
::: {.column width="40%"}

<i class='bi bi-1-circle'></i> At center, a **single *fact table*:**

* *Long*, many many rows, as few columns as possible
* "Single source of truth"

<i class='bi bi-2-circle'></i> Pointers to **dimension tables:**

* *Wide*, many many columns
* All relevant information about each **value** in the fact table

:::
::::

## Data Lake {.crunch-title .text-90}

* As data scale grows, the "up front" work required to ETL data into warehouses becomes more and more daunting...
* Data lake = drop stringent requirements of warehouse (structured tables), and just... toss data into **object storage** (**S3 buckets**)!
* [Jeff's take] Relates to **schema-on-write** vs. **schema-on-read**:
  * Can't write just anything into warehouse tables, needs to **match schema**
  * ...But, you **can** write just anything into S3 buckets
* Tossing stuff into a big lake can lead to **data swamps** 😱 ...Gives rise to **Data Lakehouse** model (Databricks)

## Data Lakehouse (Databricks)

* Still tossing data into "lake"
* **But**, data platforms like [**Databricks**](https://www.databricks.com/product/data-lakehouse) do extra work to organize it
* For example: Auto-scan the stuff tossed into the lake to populate **data catalog**
* ...AWS Glue x AWS Athena = simplest possible version of this automated data cataloging!

# AWS Athena: "Automated" ETL! {data-stack-name="Athena"}

* Carry out analytic queries **directly on S3 buckets!**
